newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia aid conference postponed - official.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia aid conference postponed - official.

text.p: A fund-raising conference for Bosnia's reconstruction set for next week has been postponed because the peacetime central government failed to adopt economic reforms in time, a World Bank official said on Friday.

"The donors' conference will not take place on June 24 and 25 as we earlier hoped for or planned. Expectations are that it will be held in the middle of July," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.

The conference, which was expected to raise $1.4 billion in reconstruction aid in 1997, has been repeatedly postponed because Bosnia's inter-ethnic government has failed to approve a package of economic laws which the international community had set down as a precondition for more aid.

Leaders of Bosnia's Serb republic withrew their support earlier this month for the economic laws which had been agreed after months of negotiations, despite threats they could lose out on substantial financial aid for their cash-strapped territory.

Bosnian Serb leaders opposed a proposed customs and tariffs law because they said it violated a cooperation agreement with neighbouring Yugoslavia. International envoys say the cooperation pact between the Serb entity and Yugoslavia carries no legal validity because Moslem and Croat members of the central government and parliament were never consulted.

A 1995 peace treaty divides Bosnia into autonomous Serb and Moslem-Croat territories which are supposed to be governed by a central presidency, cabinet and parliament. The joint institutions have been virtually paralysed since post-war elections were held last September.
